issues.description: Client is recreated per invocation; no measurement justifies the allocation cost
issues.detail: Each LLMContextFrame opens a new aioboto3 client via async with. For a streaming voice processor this is the hot path. Either cache the client at first use or state the invariant that per-call client creation is acceptable here. The author should measure before claiming this is fine; right now it is asymptotically O(N) client creations for N turns with non-trivial constants.

issues.description: default_response_to_output_transformer can raise on malformed input with no handling
issues.detail: json.loads(response_line) will raise JSONDecodeError on any non-JSON line, propagating out of process_frame and killing the pipeline. The invariant 'response is valid JSON' is assumed but never stated nor checked. Either prove the AgentCore contract guarantees this, or wrap with explicit error handling and a logged warning, parallel to the 'data: ' prefix check.

issues.description: Race condition between timeout-driven close and final close; invariant on _output_response_open not stated
issues.detail: _close_output_response_after_timeout reads and mutates _output_response_open without synchronization with _push_text_frame and the final close block. If the timeout fires between cancel_task checks, an end frame may be pushed while a new text frame is about to open one. State the invariant on _output_response_open transitions and protect it, or prove ordering via the event loop's single-threaded execution explicitly.

issues.description: agentArn parameter name violates PEP 8 and the surrounding code's own conventions
issues.detail: The constructor uses agentArn (camelCase) while every other parameter is snake_case (aws_access_key, aws_region). Code is read more than written; the reader's first reaction is 'why is this one different.' Rename to agent_arn. The AWS API field is agentRuntimeArn, but that is an internal mapping concern, not a public API choice.

issues.description: Magic number 6 for 'data: ' prefix length lacks a literate comment
issues.detail: line = line[6:] with a trailing '# omit data: ' comment is the kind of opaque slice that ages badly. Use len('data: ') or define a constant DATA_PREFIX = 'data: '. The cost is zero and the reader does not have to count characters to verify correctness. This is precisely the readability/correctness joint concern.

The field is assigned in _push_text_frame but no code consumes it; the timeout logic uses asyncio.sleep alone. Dead state confuses the reader and invites future bugs when someone assumes it carries meaning. Either remove it or use it to implement a tighter idle check that does not rely on a fresh sleep per frame.

review.summary: The processor is correct in the common case but UNDER-AUDITED on several invariants that matter for a streaming voice pipeline. The output-response bookend state machine (_output_response_open transitions across timeout task, push path, and final-close path) needs an explicit invariant comment and audit; right now correctness rests on implicit event-loop serialization. The default JSON parser will crash the pipeline on malformed lines, and the per-frame client creation is a PREMATURE-PESSIMIZATION the author should measure rather than assume. Naming and a magic number are NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT issues that cost nothing to fix.
